title: Should schools stop giving homework? A Florida district's 2017 no-homework policy and research on how much homework helps

sources.title: A Florida School District Is Eliminating Homework in Favor of Reading (Katie Reilly, 2017-07-19)
Duke Study: Homework Helps Students Succeed in School, As Long as There Isn't Too Much (2006-03)
Probing Question: Is homework bad for kids? (Alexa Stevenson, 2009-08-30)

facts.text: In 2017 the Marion County school district in Florida stopped giving traditional homework to all of its elementary school students.
Instead of homework, the Marion County elementary students were asked to read for 20 minutes every night.
The Marion County policy did not apply to middle school or high school students.
The district's new superintendent, Heidi Maier, made the decision because research suggests that reading helps young students do better in school, while traditional homework may not.
Harris Cooper, a psychology professor at Duke University, led a review of more than 60 studies on homework published between 1987 and 2003; it appeared in 2006.
The review found that students who do more homework tend to do better in school.
The link between homework and school success was much stronger for students in grades 7 to 12 than for students in elementary school.
For older high school students, doing more than about two hours of homework a night was not linked to better results.
Cooper said that giving students too much homework can work against them at every level, and that students can burn out.
A common rule of thumb, the 10-minute rule, adds about 10 minutes of homework a night for each grade, so a fourth grader would get about 40 minutes and a high school senior about two hours.
For young children, homework may mainly help them learn to manage their time and build study habits.
Cooper recommended that all students do some homework, with the amount and type depending on their age and stage of development.
Too much homework can cut into family time and can make children lose interest in school.
Many teachers give the same worksheets to every student and often do not go over the finished work.
Homework that teachers do not check or give feedback on is probably not effective.
Homework works best when it is matched to what each student still needs to learn and the teacher reviews it regularly.

notes: 兩篇投書（老師、家長）是虛構的校刊投稿，作者與學校都是虛構的；具體事件是 2017 年美國佛羅里達州 Marion County 學區小學取消傳統作業、改成每晚閱讀 20 分鐘（TIME）。研究事實取自 Duke 大學（Cooper 2006 回顧研究）與 Penn State 的報導。
